raw_case_text:
A 33-year-old female presented to the emergency department after 2 weeks of painful sore throat, fever, chills, malaise, and a pruritic rash initially on her face and arms that spread to the neck and legs. She denied conjunctivitis, arthralgia, or other associated symptoms. She had no significant past medical history and was not taking any medication. The patient had been treated in the community with a 7-day course of amoxicillin for potential bacterial tonsillitis. As her sore throat did not improve, amoxicillin was changed to cefuroxime and roxithromycin for an additional 7 days of treatment without clinical improvement and the patient was referred to our hospital.
Physical examination findings were notable for a temperature of 37.9 C, bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, grade 3 tonsillar enlargements with ulcerated pus-filled lesions on the right tonsil (Fig. 1), and multiple pseudovesicular, mammillated, edematous plaques on her neck, face, and extremities (Fig. 2). A complete blood cell count revealed leukocytosis: white blood cell count 14,250/microL (normal 4,000-11,000) with neutrophils 11,600/microL (normal 2,000-7,000). Throat, nasopharyngeal, blood, and urine cultures were negative (including Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis). Viral screening was negative for herpes simplex virus 1, herpes simplex virus 2, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and H1N1 using PCR techniques. Throat cultures for detecting group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus pyogenes and serum test for antistreptolysin-O antibodies were negative.
Syphilis serology demonstrated a Venereal Disease Research Laboratory test result of 1:32, a positive treponemal IgM/IgG antibody test, and a positive Treponema pallidum hemagglutination test. HIV p24 antibody and antigen tests were negative.
A skin biopsy specimen demonstrated a neutrophil-rich and acanthotic epidermis; a diffuse cellular infiltration of the upper dermis with a nodular tendency consisted of centrally located neutrophils, showing leukocytoclasia with admixed histiocytes and lymphocytes, plasma cells and eosinophils were absent; endothelial cell swelling and proliferation was noted but without extravasated red cells, fibrinoid necrosis of vessels, or microthrombi (Fig. 3). No microorganisms were visualized. The histological features were characteristic of Sweet syndrome, while according to the clinical and laboratory features a diagnosis of secondary syphilis was made. The patient was treated with weekly intramuscular injections of 2.4 million units of benzathine penicillin over a period of 4 weeks, followed by treatment with tapering doses of systemic prednisone (1 mg/kg/day which were gradually tapered within 2 weeks). The tonsillar lesions and the rash resolved without scarring, but with little residual pigmentation.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 33-year-old female presented with a 2-week history of severe sore throat, fever, chills, malaise, and a pruritic edematous plaque eruption over her face, neck, arms, and legs.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the preceding 2 weeks, the patient developed painful pharyngitis, fever, chills, malaise, and a pruritic rash that began on her face and arms and spread to her neck and lower extremities. She failed a 7-day outpatient course of amoxicillin followed by a 7-day course of cefuroxime plus roxithromycin for presumed bacterial tonsillitis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, malaise, severe sore throat, and pruritic pseudovesicular skin plaques; negative for conjunctivitis or arthralgia. Recent ineffective medications: amoxicillin, cefuroxime, and roxithromycin.

objective.physical_examination: Body temperature was 37.9 C. Head, neck, and cutaneous examination revealed bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, grade 3+ tonsillar hypertrophy with ulcerated, exudative/pus-filled lesions on the right tonsil, and multiple erythematous, edematous, mammillated, pseudovesicular plaques across the face, neck, and upper and lower extremities.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC showed neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC 14,250/uL [normal 4,000-11,000]; neutrophils 11,600/uL [normal 2,000-7,000]). Throat, nasopharyngeal, blood, and urine cultures and NAATs (including Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, and group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus pyogenes), serum ASO titer, viral PCR panel (HSV-1, HSV-2, EBV, CMV, H1N1 influenza), and HIV p24 Ag/Ab screening were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Skin biopsy histopathology demonstrated epidermal acanthosis with intraepidermal neutrophils and a dense, nodular upper-dermal neutrophilic infiltrate with leukocytoclasia, admixed histiocytes and lymphocytes, and endothelial swelling without true fibrinoid vasculitis or plasma cells, characteristic of Sweet syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed secondary syphilis presenting with syphilitic ulcerated tonsillitis and secondary Sweet syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis), established via reactive serum VDRL (titer 1:32), positive treponemal IgM/IgG antibody, positive TPHA, and Sweet-syndrome-like neutrophilic dermatosis on skin biopsy. Treated with intramuscular benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units once weekly for 4 weeks followed by a 2-week tapering course of oral prednisone (starting at 1 mg/kg/day), resulting in complete resolution of both the tonsillar ulcers and pseudovesicular skin plaques without scarring.
